source: ETIS Engineering Platform Starter Kit v1.0.0

items.title: ES-100 — Engineering Principles
items.why: Foundational principles include governance as architecture and the rule that everything important leaves evidence.
items.student_hint: Look at ES-100 Engineering Principles, especially governance, escalation, decision rights, and durable evidence.

items.title: ES-101 — Engineering Context
items.why: Explains why early scope, stakeholder, accountability, and decision boundaries constrain later engineering work.
items.student_hint: Review ES-101 Engineering Context when the issue is about scope, stakeholders, early decisions, or why an unresolved beginning matters downstream.

items.title: ES-102 — Requirements and Constraints
items.why: Provides requirements, constraints, evidence, and readiness guidance that feeds planning decisions.
items.student_hint: Use ES-102 when you need to determine whether requirements or constraints are sufficiently clear to support a planning claim.

items.title: ES-103 — Planning and Work Breakdown
items.why: Treats planning as accountable evidence and emphasizes uncertainty, dependencies, review, rework, governance, and decision points.
items.student_hint: Look at ES-103 Engineering Context for planning, ownership, uncertainty, dependencies, and re-estimation.

items.title: LMU/COICP — Roles and Responsibilities Example
items.why: Shows concrete responsibility and evidence ownership in a completed professional example.
items.student_hint: The LMU/COICP Roles and Responsibilities example shows how responsibility and evidence ownership can be made explicit. Use it as an example, not an answer to copy.

items.title: LMU/COICP — Repository Conventions Example
items.why: Demonstrates how decisions, risks, AI use, requirements, release, and governance remain durable and traceable.
items.student_hint: The LMU/COICP Repository Conventions example can help you see what durable engineering evidence looks like across a lifecycle.

items.title: ES-104 — Architecture
items.why: Architecture guidance for boundaries, responsibilities, dependencies, tradeoffs, and reviewability.
items.student_hint: Use ES-104 when the review turns on architecture boundaries, responsibilities, dependencies, or consequences of a design choice.

items.title: ES-106 through ES-109 — Implementation, Review, Integration, Verification
items.why: Implementation and verification guidance for controlled change, review, integration, and evidence.
items.student_hint: For A4, use the relevant ES-106 through ES-109 stage guidance for implementation readiness, review, integration, and verification.

items.title: ES-109 / ES-110 — Validation and Release Readiness
items.why: Supports evidence-backed release judgment, validation, limitations, and readiness decisions.
items.student_hint: Use ES-109 and ES-110 when the question is whether evidence is strong enough to defend a Cycle 1 release.

items.title: ES-110 through ES-114 — Release, Operations, Monitoring, Learning, Stewardship
items.why: Supports final operational readiness, governance, monitoring, recovery, learning, and stewardship judgment.
items.student_hint: For A6, use the relevant ES-110 through ES-114 guidance to reason about release, operations, monitoring, recovery, and stewardship.
